text:
opsbot: ALERT — us-west1: ephemeral NVMe read error rate >5% over 5m, GPU attach latency spike, some provision requests falling back to reserved/dedicated pools. https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/7543210987 :eyes:

alex_m: seeing this too, a bunch of batch gpu jobs stalled at 'waiting for local disk'. Attach retries then fallback to dedicated pool which inflated cost. Anyone owning scrub/janitor today?

jenn_storage: that looks like our scrub window overlapped with a heavy batch launch wave. nodes in scratchpool-3 showed concurrent fstrim + deep-scrub, causing IOPS blowout and driver read-retries. quick grep from node-34: ```kernel: nvme0: read error, status: DNR
kernel: nvme nvme0n1: I/O 1234 failed, retrying
```

sara_oncall: we had a brief network fabric flapping in us-west1 ~ 02:58 UTC which could have amplified read-retry backpressure. if attachments are waiting longer, autoscaler is deciding to go to dedicated to satisfy timeliness. :fire:

alex_m: cost impact is real — we saw provisioning fallback count +120 in last 2h and dedicated attach rate up. Can we pause scrub on affected pools and throttle janitor? Also want to reduce premature dedicated fallback while we triage.

marta_cost: current burn estimate: ~+$9k last 3 hours because of reserved fallback and short-lived dedicated bursts. If fallback persists, weekly run-rate could be +$50k. Please consider cost guard. :money_with_wings:

kai_infra: short plan: 1) temporarily pause deep-scrub on scratchpool-3 (storage), 2) change attach policy to add linear backoff/retry so we avoid immediate dedicated fallback, 3) enable cross-region soft-failover for non-prod to eu-west1 for batch. I can push the attach policy flag behind a feature toggle.

jenn_storage: pausing deep-scrub now on pool scratchpool-3. Will switch to lightweight scrub (metadata-only) for next 90m and stagger the remaining scrub jobs. Also opening an ops-PR to add a small jitter to scrub start times.

alex_m: thanks. For attach policy change: what's the safe timeout increase? We don't want to hang user-facing workloads.

kai_infra: propose: increase attach timeout from 6s -> 18s with exponential backoff (3 retries) for batch/non-interactive paths. For interactive routes keep current 6s. Example flag curl: ```curl -XPOST https://infra-api/flags -d '{"attach_timeout":18, "attach_retries":3, "scope":"batch"}'``` will be behind FF so we can revert.

sara_oncall: I'll patch oncall runbook to watch GPU-attach-latency and nvme-read-error-rate. If nvme errors drop after scrub pause, revert the backoff after stabilization.

marta_cost: please add an automated cost-alert if dedicated-fallback spend > $2k/hr for next 24h. I can create the guard and give infra rights to mute during mitigation windows.

jenn_storage: also filing a firmware correlation ticket — some nodes show increased controller resets during the scrub window. If we confirm firmware interactions, schedule a staggered firmware application and coordinate with provisioning windows.

kai_infra: creating short-lived autoscaler config change and feature flag now, will post PR link. Rolling to canary nodes first (10%).

opsbot: Created tasks — TICKET-6532 pause-scrub-scratchpool-3, TICKET-6533 attach-backoff-flag, TICKET-6534 cross-region-soft-failover. Monitoring dashboards updated.

alex_m: action owners: jenn_storage pause + scrub jitter (done), kai_infra feature flag PR + canary, sara_oncall monitor and coordinate, marta_cost cost guard. Follow up in 45m.

sara_oncall: acknowledged, will escalate if IOPS or attach latencies do not improve within 30m.

jenn_storage: scrub pause confirmed on affected nodes, starting lightweight pass. Will post before/after IOPS graph link in 20m.

kai_infra: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/flags/pull/189 — starting canary deploy to 10% attach traffic now.

opsbot: UPDATE — attach-backoff flag active on canary. Metrics: attach latency median increased to 4s (still below interactive threshold), dedicated-fallback count on canary reduced by 78%.

alex_m: nice. keep an eye on errors continuing to appear (if read errors persist we may need to evict bad nodes). Good work team. :thumbsup:
